subject.title: fix(doctor): warn when maxActiveTranscriptBytes is set without truncateAfterCompaction

question: Should default `openclaw doctor --lint` warn and return a finding for existing positive `maxActiveTranscriptBytes` settings when `truncateAfterCompaction` is disabled?
rationale: The source and docs establish that this setting combination leaves the guard inactive, but making Doctor flag it by default changes existing automation-visible lint results rather than only correcting runtime behavior.

options.title: Accept the default warning
options.body: Treat the documented inactive configuration as a default Doctor lint warning, preserving runtime behavior while making the ineffective setting visible.

options.title: Make the check opt-in
options.body: Keep the diagnostic available only through an explicit Doctor selection so existing default lint gates remain unchanged.

options.title: Pause for broader Doctor policy
options.body: Defer the check until maintainers define whether default Doctor findings should cover documented-but-inactive optional settings.

recommendation.title: Accept the default warning
recommendation.body: Treat the documented inactive configuration as a default Doctor lint warning, preserving runtime behavior while making the ineffective setting visible.

likelyOwner.reason: The original compaction work established the setting dependency and is the closest available ownership signal for deciding its Doctor policy.
